# R6 · Turns, lane changes, passing & roundabouts: questions

**Rules half** · 26 questions · [Study guide](../guide/R6-turns-lanes-passing.md) · [All rules topics](../README.md)

Answers are hidden. Tap **Answer** under each question to check yourself.

---

### 1. To make a U-turn, you must be able to see at least how far in both directions?

*Exact numbers*

- **A.** 300 metres
- **B.** 100 metres
- **C.** 50 metres
- **D.** 150 metres

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. 150 metres**

Never make a U-turn unless you can see at least 150 m both ways.

> 📖 Handbook: "Never make a U-turn unless you can see at least 150 metres in both directions."

</details>

---

### 2. You may not pass left of the centre line within how many metres of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel?

*Exact numbers*

- **A.** 100 metres
- **B.** 30 metres
- **C.** 10 metres
- **D.** 50 metres

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. 30 metres**

30 m: the same as the no-passing distance at a pedestrian crossover.

> 📖 Handbook: "Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel."

</details>

---

### 3. It is illegal to drive in reverse on a divided road with a speed limit over…

*Exact numbers*

- **A.** 80 km/h
- **B.** 100 km/h
- **C.** 50 km/h
- **D.** 60 km/h

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A. 80 km/h**

That includes the shoulder. The only exception is helping someone in trouble.

> 📖 Handbook: "It is illegal to drive in reverse on a divided road that has a speed limit of more than 80 km/h."

</details>

---

### 4. You're driving inside a roundabout. A car is waiting at the yield line to enter. Who has the right-of-way?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Whoever is on the right
- **B.** The entering car
- **C.** You do: don't stop except to avoid a collision
- **D.** Whoever is bigger

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. You do: don't stop except to avoid a collision**

Once you're in the roundabout, you have the right-of-way over entering traffic.

> 📖 Handbook: "Once you are in the roundabout, do not stop except to avoid a collision; you have the right-of-way over entering traffic."

</details>

---

### 5. You signal to change lanes. Must drivers in the other lane let you in?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Yes, a signal gives you the right-of-way
- **B.** Yes, if you signal for 3 seconds
- **C.** Only if they're slower than you
- **D.** No: they expect you to stay in your lane and to yield to them

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. No: they expect you to stay in your lane and to yield to them**

Even if you signal, other drivers expect you to yield the right-of-way.

> 📖 Handbook: "Even if you signal, they expect you to yield the right-of-way."

</details>

---

### 6. On a two-lane road, a car is passing you in the oncoming lane, and oncoming traffic is getting close. What should you do?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Move left to block the passer
- **B.** Move to the right side of your lane and be ready to slow down to let the passing car in
- **C.** Keep your speed and position
- **D.** Speed up so the passer drops back

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Move to the right side of your lane and be ready to slow down to let the passing car in**

Help the passing driver get in front of you quickly to prevent a collision.

> 📖 Handbook: "Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision."

</details>

---

### 7. You've stopped at a red light and want to turn right. A pedestrian is starting to cross in front of you. What do you do?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Honk so they wait
- **B.** Turn, since right on red is allowed
- **C.** Wait for the pedestrian, then turn when the way is clear
- **D.** Turn quickly before they reach your lane

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Wait for the pedestrian, then turn when the way is clear**

Right on red: complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and other road users.

> 📖 Handbook: "Remember to signal your turn and yield to pedestrians and others using the road."

</details>

---

### 8. You're turning left from a one-way road onto a one-way road at a red light. Who must you yield to?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Only buses
- **B.** Only vehicles turning right
- **C.** Pedestrians and traffic
- **D.** No one; you have the right-of-way

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Pedestrians and traffic**

Stop completely, then yield to pedestrians and traffic before turning.

> 📖 Handbook: "You may turn left from a one-way road to a one-way road on a red light after coming to a complete stop and making sure the way is clear. Yield to pedestrians and traffic."

</details>

---

### 9. You're waiting in a two-way left-turn lane. An oncoming car is waiting in the same lane, in front of you, and blocks your view. What should you do?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Turn quickly while the other car waits
- **B.** Turn only when you are sure the way is clear
- **C.** Pass the other car in the centre lane
- **D.** Back up to see better

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Turn only when you are sure the way is clear**

Cars from both directions use this lane. Only go when you're sure.

> 📖 Handbook: "Only go when you are sure the way is clear."

</details>

---

### 10. On a highway where trucks can't use the far left lane, you're in the next lane over and a truck wants to pass. What should you do?

*Right-of-way*

- **A.** Stay in your lane; the truck must wait
- **B.** Move to the far left lane
- **C.** Move to the right-hand lane as soon as you can
- **D.** Speed up so the truck can't pass

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Move to the right-hand lane as soon as you can**

That lane is the truck passing lane.

> 📖 Handbook: "If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can."

</details>

---

### 11. When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:

*Right-of-way* ⭐ *Official MTO sample question*

- **A.** Signal to the other driver not to pass.
- **B.** Move to the left to prevent passing.
- **C.** Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.
- **D.** Speed up so that passing is not necessary.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.**

Official MTO sample question. Never speed up when being passed.

> 📖 Handbook: "When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety."

</details>

---

### 12. When may you pass on the RIGHT shoulder?

*Word traps*

- **A.** Only to pass a vehicle turning left, and only if the shoulder is paved
- **B.** Any time traffic is slow
- **C.** Whenever the shoulder is wide enough
- **D.** Never

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A. Only to pass a vehicle turning left, and only if the shoulder is paved**

Right shoulder: only around a left-turning vehicle, only if paved. Left shoulder: never.

> 📖 Handbook: "You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved."

</details>

---

### 13. When may you pass on the LEFT shoulder?

*Word traps*

- **A.** Only in an emergency
- **B.** Only to pass a vehicle turning right
- **C.** Never
- **D.** Only if it's paved

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Never**

You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

> 📖 Handbook: "You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not."

</details>

---

### 14. Which of these is NOT a time when passing on the right is allowed?

*Word traps*

- **A.** On a multi-lane road
- **B.** On a two-lane, two-way road when the car ahead is slow
- **C.** On a one-way road
- **D.** When overtaking a left-turning vehicle

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. On a two-lane, two-way road when the car ahead is slow**

Passing on the right is allowed on multi-lane or one-way roads, and when passing a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

> 📖 Handbook: "You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle."

</details>

---

### 15. Do you have to wear your seatbelt while backing up?

*Word traps*

- **A.** Yes, always
- **B.** Only on a highway
- **C.** No: you may take it off to turn and see, but buckle up before driving forward
- **D.** Only if you have passengers

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. No: you may take it off to turn and see, but buckle up before driving forward**

It's one of the few times you may remove it, if you need to turn your body to see.

> 📖 Handbook: "You don't have to wear a seatbelt while backing up."

</details>

---

### 16. Which of these is NOT allowed inside a roundabout?

*Word traps*

- **A.** Signalling before your exit
- **B.** Changing lanes
- **C.** Driving counter-clockwise
- **D.** Watching for pedestrians as you exit

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Changing lanes**

Don't change lanes in a roundabout. If you miss your exit, go around again.

> 📖 Handbook: "Do not change lanes while in the roundabout."

</details>

---

### 17. Never change lanes in traffic without:

*Word traps* ⭐ *Official MTO sample question*

- **A.** Decreasing speed and giving correct signal.
- **B.** Giving proper signal and looking to make sure the move can be made safely.
- **C.** Blowing your horn and looking to the rear.
- **D.** Looking in the rear view mirror only.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Giving proper signal and looking to make sure the move can be made safely.**

Official MTO sample question. Mirror only isn't enough: shoulder check too.

> 📖 Handbook: "Never change lanes without giving the proper signal and looking to make sure the move can be made safely."

</details>

---

### 18. You're stopped in the intersection, waiting to turn left. How should your front wheels be?

*Best action*

- **A.** Turned right, to be safe
- **B.** It doesn't matter
- **C.** Turned left, ready to go
- **D.** Straight, until you can actually make the turn

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. Straight, until you can actually make the turn**

If you're hit from behind with your wheels turned left, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

> 📖 Handbook: "When you are stopped at an intersection waiting for approaching traffic to clear, don't turn your steering wheel to the left until you can complete the turn."

</details>

---

### 19. To keep full control when turning a corner, when should you finish braking?

*Best action*

- **A.** You shouldn't brake for turns
- **B.** After you finish the turn
- **C.** Before you turn the steering wheel
- **D.** While you turn the wheel

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Before you turn the steering wheel**

Try not to brake and steer at the same time.

> 📖 Handbook: "To keep full control of the vehicle, finish braking before you turn the steering wheel."

</details>

---

### 20. After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into its lane?

*Best action*

- **A.** When the other driver flashes their lights
- **B.** After counting to two
- **C.** As soon as your back bumper is past its front bumper
- **D.** When you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside (rear-view) mirror

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. When you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside (rear-view) mirror**

Signal first, then return once its whole front shows in your rear-view mirror.

> 📖 Handbook: "when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you are passing in your inside mirror, make the lane change"

</details>

---

### 21. You're in the inside lane of a roundabout and you miss your exit. What should you do?

*Best action*

- **A.** Change lanes quickly and exit
- **B.** Stop and wait for a gap to cut across
- **C.** Back up to the exit
- **D.** Keep going around until you reach your exit again

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. Keep going around until you reach your exit again**

Don't stop and don't change lanes in a roundabout.

> 📖 Handbook: "If in the inside lane and you miss your exit, you must continue around until you meet your exit again."

</details>

---

### 22. You missed your turn. What is the simplest and safest way to turn around?

*Best action*

- **A.** Make a three-point turn on a hill
- **B.** Back up to the turn
- **C.** Drive around the block
- **D.** Make a U-turn on a curve

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Drive around the block**

If driving around the block isn't possible, a U-turn or three-point turn may be needed.

> 📖 Handbook: "The simplest and safest way is to drive around the block"

</details>

---

### 23. Where is it illegal to make a U-turn?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** Only on freeways
- **B.** On a curve, on or near a railway crossing or hilltop, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view
- **C.** Anywhere in a city
- **D.** On any road with two lanes

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. On a curve, on or near a railway crossing or hilltop, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view**

These places block your view. Also never where a sign says no U-turn.

> 📖 Handbook: "It is illegal to make a U-turn on a curve in the road, on or near a railway crossing or hilltop, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view."

</details>

---

### 24. How must you pass a streetcar?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** On the left
- **B.** Never: wait behind it
- **C.** On the right, unless you're on a one-way road
- **D.** On either side

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. On the right, unless you're on a one-way road**

Pass streetcars on the right (except on one-way roads).

> 📖 Handbook: "You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road."

</details>

---

### 25. At a roundabout, you want to turn left. Which lane should you use?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** The right lane
- **B.** The left lane
- **C.** Either lane
- **D.** The lane with less traffic

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. The left lane**

Left lane = turn left or go straight. Right lane = turn right or go straight.

> 📖 Handbook: "Use the left lane to turn left or to go straight."

</details>

---

### 26. When you are deciding whether or not to make a U-turn, your first consideration should be to check:

*Laws & consequences* ⭐ *Official MTO sample question*

- **A.** Turning radius of your car.
- **B.** Height of curb.
- **C.** Presence of trees, fire hydrants or poles near the curb.
- **D.** Traffic regulations.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. Traffic regulations.**

Official MTO sample question. First make sure there's no sign forbidding it.

> 📖 Handbook: "Before you make a U-turn, check to make sure there is no sign saying not to."

</details>
